newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Non-oil data cheers up Singapore shares at noon.
newsitem.headline: Non-oil data cheers up Singapore shares at noon.

text.p: A 5.9 percent rise in April non-oil domestic exports compared to the same period last year cheered up the Singapore stock market on Tuesday, dealers said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index moved up to 19.52 points to 2,070.46 in the last 30 minutes before the midday break after hovering in the 2,056 region.
"It's a positive number being on the higher end of expectations.
"We will see some buying of index stocks and blue chips from those who have held back orders pending the data's release," said T.K Yap, director of institutional sales at Ong & Co.

Yap emphasised it was more a case of short-term improved sentiment rather than a real shift of funds. "Investors will want to look at the numbers more closely. One number does not make a trend," he said.
Dealers said the market should stay firm in the afternoon with the key index aiming at 2,080. Property stocks got a further lift with its index surging 2.43 percent to 694.16.

CityDev jumped Singapore $0.40 to S$12.90. Foreign tranches of UOB, OCBC and OUB gained between S$0.40 and S$0.25. Market volume was 74 million shares with 273 advances clobbering 48 declines. --Josephine Ng (65-8703094)
